column4: Pixel-art game character sprites in exactly the same style as the reference image: the same pixel size, the same palette and shading, the same rough grain, noise and dither, sallow slightly wrong skin tones and stiff, vacant, unsettling faces. Two figures of the SAME person side by side on one sheet, with a wide gap of background between them so they do not touch, both at exactly the same size and scale, each filling about 85% of the height, the feet touching the bottom edge. LEFT: standing facing the viewer, arms hanging at the sides. RIGHT: the same person seen from the front working at a counter that is NOT drawn, both forearms forward at waist height, the hands busy just below the waist, the head bowed looking down at the work. The person: a heavy woman of about sixty with wavy grey hair, a broad tired face, a cream blouse under a white kitchen smock with old brown stains, a white apron tied over it, thick flesh-coloured stockings, worn brown slip-on shoes. Nothing in the hands but a dishcloth. Something about this person is subtly off, like a stranger you would not sit next to. No smile, not cheerful, not clean or cartoonish, the same uncomfortable proportions as the reference. The background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around the figures, no counter, no table, no floor, no ground shadow, no text, no border, no watermark.
